title: Guided fallback scripting scratchbook
content:
Notes to self: quick dump of guided fallback scripting idea and experiments. Rough — not polished.

Context:
- We keep seeing customer questions about predictable behavior when a primary model is unavailable or underperforming. Current platform-level fallbacks are model/region-based and fairly rigid.
- Need a way product teams can author small scripts/policies that guide fallback behavior without touching infra: combine QoS signals, prompt transforms, and routing decisions.

Idea summary (one-liner):
- A lightweight "guided fallback script" sandbox where product/solution engineers author compact rules that control: model substitution, prompt adaptation (trim/boost/clarify), staged retry backoffs, and cost-tier downgrades. Script deploys as a named policy attached to a route/canary.

Key goals: 
- Predictable, auditable behavior when things degrade.
- Low-friction authoring for non-infra engineers.
- Safe by default: sandboxed, rated-limited, with dry-run and explainability.

Constraints / guiding principles:
- Scripts must be declarative or a tiny DSL, not full Turing-complete code.
- Execution must be bounded (time/tokens) and traceable.
- Hooks only into routing layer and prompt transform pipeline (no arbitrary secrets access).

User personas:
- Product engineer (needs to ship a canary that downgrades gracefully when latency spikes).
- Solutions engineer (customer request for per-tenant fallback behavior).
- SRE (wants predictable, detectable policies and metrics).

Rough UX flow:
1) Author policy in console sandbox (modal): choose triggers (latency threshold, error rate, quality regression score, cost-burn), choose actions (model switch, template injection, response length cap, quick follow-up prompt to clarify), set cooldowns and max-fallbacks.
2) Dry-run mode: simulate on recorded traces, preview transformed prompt + selected model variant.
3) Attach to route/version/canary.
4) Live: policy logs show decisions and explainers for each request affected (token-limited).

Toy DSL sketch (very rough):
- trigger {metric: latency_p95, op: ">", value: 350, window: 60s} -> action {type: model_switch, target: "m-small-q4", reason: "latency_p95>350ms"} 
- fallback {if quality_score < 0.7 then transform_prompt: "append: 'Focus only on steps, be concise'"; retry: {attempts: 1, delay_ms: 150}}

Example user stories (prioritized):
- US1: As a product engineer, I can attach a guided fallback policy to a route so that during latency spikes the route switches to a lower-latency quantized variant.
  - Acceptance: policy applied within 5s of trigger detection; logs show which requests were routed.
- US2: As a solutions engineer, I can create a policy that shortens prompts and reduces max_tokens when cost budget per-session exceeds X.
  - Acceptance: transformed prompts are visible in dry-run; billing shows reduced token counts.
- US3: As an SRE, I can view real-time metrics for how often policies fire and alert when fallback rate exceeds threshold.
  - Acceptance: dashboard tile + alert rule present.

Operational/implementation notes:
- Policy evaluation should be on the request path but minimal overhead: precompiled decision tree, compiled at deploy time.
- Use existing telemetry signals (p95, error rate, regression alerts) via metrics API.
- Transformations are templated operations (truncate, prepend, append, redact, replace placeholders). Avoid ad-hoc string code.
- Rollout: start with hosted API routes only, opt-in beta.

Experiments to run (alpha):
- E1: Measure latency overhead of policy engine across 10k reqs with simple model_switch rules. Target <1ms added p99.
- E2: Dry-run fidelity: compare dry-run predicted routing vs actual runtime across 24h; goal: >95% match.
- E3: Business impact A/B: routes with simple prompt-trim fallback vs routes without; measure tokens/latency/complaint signal.

Metrics to track:
- policy_fire_rate (per-policy)
- avg_added_latency_ms (policy eval)
- fallback_success_rate (fallback requests that meet initial SLO)
- token_delta_pct (before/after transform)
- customer_complaints / regained_quality_score

Safety & governance:
- Policies require role-based approval for production attach.
- Audit log with request-level explainers (capped).
- Rejection/validation rules: deny transforms that remove safety-related prompts or redact required context.

Edge cases / open questions:
- How to test policies for hybrid fallbacks (model + prompt + sample-size)?
- Tenant-specific policies vs global — how to prioritize? (order precedence needed)
- How to handle chained fallbacks (prevent infinite degradation loops)?
- What happens when policy engine itself errors? (must fail-safe to primary route)

Data & infra considerations:
- Need a small persisted artifact for each policy (compiled form).
- Telemetry integration: tag traces with policy_id and decision path.
- Storage for dry-run logs (maybe 7 days default).

Possible MVP scope (minimal):
- DSL supporting: model_switch, prompt_truncate, prepend_template, cooldown, simple retry.
- Console authoring + dry-run against last 1000 trace samples.
- Logging and a small dashboard tile.

Longer term / nice-to-have:
- Conditional probability-based routing using quality model predictions.
- Per-customer policy library with templates.
- Policy simulator with cost/latency forecasting.

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Talk to SRE early about performance guardrails (E1).
- Draft RFC for a minimal DSL and vet with legal on redaction rules.
- Mock console authoring flow (3 screens) — ask Maya for quick sketches.
- Create JIRA epic (linked_artifacts placeholder).

Random braindump ideas:
- Offer a guided "quick fallback" wizard: choose a scenario (latency / cost / quality) -> present three recommended policy templates.
- Add a telemetry-derived suggestion engine that proposes policies when we detect repeated transient regression patterns.

References / related tickets:
- JIRA-8482: customer request: per-tenant fallback when small-model is acceptable
- CONFLUENCE-FF-42: notes on graceful degradation patterns
- github PR: rollout heuristics discussion (see linked_artifacts)

End of scratchbook. Keep quick — iterate next session with Maya + SRE.
